analyst.summary: Tata Consumer's FY26 numbers look strong on the surface - 15% revenue growth, margins up, profit up over 20% - but much of that momentum is coming from smaller, newer businesses (Sampann foods, Capital Foods, Organic India, and a Starbucks joint venture that is finally narrowing its losses) rather than the core tea business, where volumes grew just 4% last quarter with no real pricing power, and the UK Tetley business is shrinking. The stock trades at a rich ~70 times earnings for a business earning only about 7-7.5% on its equity, well below peers like HUL and ITC - the market is betting on margins and returns improving substantially over the next few years. We rate it a Hold: the improvement is real but not yet proven at scale, and the next quarterly result (due 24 July 2026) is an important test of whether that improvement continues.
